issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method named checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon to process and serve orders, but the provided solution implements this behavior in a method named processOrders() instead. This name mismatch between the specification (checkOrderReady) and the solution (processOrders) is structural: students will be instructed to implement or call checkOrderReady(), and tests or graders expecting that exact method name would not find it. This inconsistency can confuse students about the required API and cause integration or grading failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() that delegates to processOrders(). Ensure the template/specification, solution, and tests consistently reference the same method name (checkOrderReady) so students implement the expected API.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named checkOrderReady() that should be invoked to try serving queued orders, but the solution implementation provides an equivalent method named processOrders(). This naming divergence (checkOrderReady vs processOrders) creates a mapping confusion for students: they will look for or be instructed to implement checkOrderReady() while the provided reference uses a different identifier for the same behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names across artifacts. Rename processOrders() in the solution to checkOrderReady(), or add a checkOrderReady() wrapper that calls processOrders(), and ensure the template/problem instructions reference the same method name so students can clearly map the requirement to the implementation.
